The submitted answer claims that the lower sums converging to the integral forces λ(P_n) → 0, which amounts to "Yes".

Check with Thomae's function on [0,1]. Every subinterval contains irrationals where f = 0, so every lower Darboux sum is 0. Also f ≥ 0 and the upper sums can be made arbitrarily small, so the integral is 0. Every subinterval contains rationals where f > 0, so f is not constant on any open subinterval. The hypothesis then holds for every sequence of partitions. Taking P_n = {0,1} for all n gives λ(P_n) = 1, which does not tend to 0.

So the correct answer is "No", and the submitted answer ("Yes") is wrong.
